questions.question: How does control flow work in Ruby?
questions.title: Control Flow in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Conditionals: if/elsif/else/end, unless (= if not), case/when (case x; when 1..5 then 'small'; when String then 'str'; else 'other'; end), and the modifier form (puts 'hi' if verbose). Loops: while, until, but Ruby prefers iterators — 10.times { |i| ... }, array.each { |x| ... }, 1.upto(5) { |n| ... }, map, select. break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current; retry (in rescue) re-runs the block. return exits the method (implicit return = last expression). Exceptions: raise throws, begin/rescue/else/ensure/end catches (rescue StandardError => e), ensure always runs. Use iterators over while counters; use case/when over long if/elsif chains; use rescue for expected errors, not normal flow.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know if/unless/case, that Ruby prefers iterators over while, and break/next/redo plus raise/rescue/ensure.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using a while counter when each/times would do, or rescue for normal control flow (it's for errors).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Control flow: if/elsif/else, unless, case/when; iterators (each/times/upto) over while; break/next/redo; raise/rescue/else/ensure.

sections.title: Branch, Loop, Handle
sections.content: Conditionals: if, elsif, else, end, unless (equals if not), case when (case x; when 1 to 5 then small; when String then str; else other; end), and the modifier form (puts hi if verbose). Loops: while, until, but Ruby prefers iterators — 10 dot times, array dot each, 1 dot upto 5, map, select. break exits a loop; next skips to the next iteration; redo retries the current; retry (in rescue) re-runs the block. return exits the method (implicit return equals last expression). Exceptions: raise throws, begin rescue else ensure end catches (rescue StandardError e), ensure always runs. Use iterators over while counters; use case when over long if elsif chains; use rescue for expected errors, not normal flow.

sections.title: Control Flow
sections.content:
if/unless/case; iterators over while; break/next/redo; raise/rescue/ensure.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[conditionals] --> I[if/elsif/else]
  C --> Ca[case/when]
  L[loops] --> It[iterators each/times]
  L --> B[break/next/redo]
  E[errors] --> R[raise/rescue/ensure]
```

sections.title: Control flow
sections.content:
```ruby
# Conditionals
if score > 90; 'A'; elsif score > 80; 'B'; else; 'C'; end
puts 'done' unless running        # unless = if NOT
puts 'hi' if verbose               # modifier form
case x
when 1..5     then 'small'
when String   then 'string'
else 'other'
end

# Loops (prefer ITERATORS over while)
3.times { |i| puts i }             # 0 1 2
[10, 20].each { |x| puts x }       # 10 20
1.upto(5) { |n| puts n }           # 1..5
nums.map { |n| n * 2 }             # transform

# while/until (less idiomatic):
i = 0
while i < 3; puts i; i += 1; end

# break (exit), next (skip), redo (retry current)
[1,2,3].each do |n|
  next if n == 2      # skip 2
  break if n > 10     # stop
  redo                 # retry this iteration (careful!)
end

# Exceptions
begin
  risky
rescue StandardError => e
  log(e.message)
else
  puts 'no error'
ensure
  cleanup             # ALWAYS runs
end

# raise throws:  raise 'bad input'
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using a while counter when each/times would do (un-idiomatic).
Using rescue for normal control flow (it's for expected errors).
Forgetting ensure (always runs; needed for cleanup).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Conditionals: if/elsif/else, unless (= if not), case/when, modifier form.
Loops: while/until, but Ruby prefers iterators (each/times/upto/map).
break exits; next skips; redo retries the current; retry (in rescue) re-runs.
return exits the method; implicit return = the last expression.
raise throws; begin/rescue/else/ensure/end catches; ensure always runs.
